correctness.rationale: Pointwise evaluator is Theorem 11 of arxiv:1608.05657. The finite 16-state binary digit Markov chain is doubly stochastic, irreducible, and aperiodic, giving uniform high-digit statistics. A complete binary-prefix partition treats the 26 ordinary words and three exceptional residue classes with first-zero position k; congruence data are periodic in k modulo four. The resulting convergent geometric sum is evaluated with exact fractions to all 64 entries. Uniform dyadic-block convergence and block decomposition prove ordinary natural density; disallowed transitions are absent from every prefix case, not just negligible. Packaged checker replays exact 16-state graph, 4096 direct recurrence indices and rational 8x8 table; no finite test is invoked as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The modular Motzkin sequence is a natural, previously investigated automatic arithmetic sequence. Knowing individual congruence classifications does not determine its neighboring residue correlations without full two-point enumeration and limit calculation. The exact 64-entry joint measure, five universally forbidden neighboring pairs despite individually positive marginals, and complete support size 44 form a motivated exhaustive arithmetic correlation invariant. The contrast mu(4,4)=0 against marginal 1/6 is a substantial structural dependence, not a trivial substitution or arbitrary slice.
